title: feat(config): configure gnome-libsecret password store for VS Code
head: de575fd3af44
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates
decision: publishable pending outer-assistant freshness and posting authorization

leads.summary: The new default is not propagated to an existing Quattro user's config
leads.consequence: A user who already has VS Code but did not install it with Omarchy's installer, and has no existing password-store override, receives only /etc/skel/.config/code-flags.conf on a package update. Their existing ~/.config/code-flags.conf stays absent, so the AUR launcher still supplies no flag and the intended Hyprland authentication fix does not arrive. The Omarchy VS Code installer is a different, already-functional path: it writes ~/.vscode/argv.json with the same pin. An explicit omarchy-refresh-config code-flags.conf or destructive omarchy-reinstall-configs can add the file, but neither runs on an ordinary update. A pre-Quattro user upgrading with omarchy-upgrade-to-quattro does receive a missing file, provided that upgrade uses the PR's packaged config tree.

leads.summary: The global code-flags.conf also changes Arch code-oss, not just Microsoft's VS Code
leads.consequence: Arch's code-oss package installs a code-oss launcher (and code symlink) which reads precisely code-flags.conf and appends its lines. On a KDE session with previously stored code-oss secrets in KWallet, seeding this config or explicitly resetting Omarchy defaults changes the selected backend to libsecret even when VS Code was never installed; the existing KWallet-encrypted tokens may no longer decrypt, and without a usable Secret Service the new key cannot initialize. Existing argv.json user overrides can take precedence; the impact applies when no such override is present. This also persists after removing Microsoft's Code because no removal of the globally seeded file accompanies its package removal. If the intended target is only visual-studio-code-bin, scope the pin to that installer's existing argv.json or explicitly consider code-oss credentials and migration.
leads.triage: dropped: outside Omarchy Hyprland sessions; requires KDE plus code-oss plus existing KWallet credentials; not verified

leads.summary: An alternate XDG_CONFIG_HOME bypasses the seeded file
leads.consequence: If a fresh account or an existing user sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME to a path other than ~/.config, omarchy-settings seeds the new file into ~/.config but the AUR VS Code wrapper looks in $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/code-flags.conf, so the new file is ignored. The alternative Omarchy VS Code installer writes ~/.vscode/argv.json and still pins the store in its normal nonportable setup, so this gap affects users relying on this PR's file rather than that installer. A matching refresh command also writes to ~/.config, not the overridden path. Either document the fixed-home convention and supported environment, or ensure this setting reaches the config path the actual launcher uses.
leads.triage: dropped: Omarchy never sets XDG_CONFIG_HOME (Opus source check); niche

leads.summary: On the normal Omarchy VS Code install route this flag duplicates an existing override
leads.consequence: omarchy-install-editor-vscode already writes password-store=gnome-libsecret to ~/.vscode/argv.json immediately after installing visual-studio-code-bin. VS Code 1.139.1 reads that file at startup and appends the same Electron command-line switch; it also overwrites an existing value of that switch. Thus this PR is not what fixes persistence for users taking the normal menu/default-editor install route, and merely adds a second source of the flag there. The new config is relevant for manual installs without the existing argv.json override. Clarify the intended target or consolidate where Omarchy configures the backend.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (observation 2); corroboration; argv.json override verified in source by both

limits: These are source-traced conditional behaviours, not execution reproductions or evidence of a user's actual stored credentials; no private desktop, keyring, or VS Code was launched.

The vendored Electron 43 synchronous OSCrypt selector and the new asynchronous FreedesktopSecretKeyProvider have different behaviour for DESKTOP_ENVIRONMENT_OTHER; synchronous safeStorage matters to VS Code 1.139.1, so do not infer redundancy from the asynchronous provider's OTHER case.

flags.claim: Impact: Remote Tunnels and serve-web stop working for every account seeded with the file
flags.why: The evidence covers the `code tunnel ...` and `code serve-web ...` commands run through the /usr/bin/code wrapper. When Remote Tunnel Access is turned on inside the editor, VS Code starts `<install>/bin/code-tunnel` directly and does not go through the wrapper. It also applies only to accounts that use these commands with visual-studio-code-bin. My report said 'users of the Remote Tunnels and serve-web CLI'; the CLI qualifier was lost.
flags.disposition: real error: impact dropped 'CLI' qualifier; fixed to name the commands

flags.claim: The new file ships only through `/etc/skel`, so it reaches new accounts but not existing Quattro installs
flags.why: omarchy-settings also installs config/** to /usr/share/omarchy/config. The one-time v3-to-Quattro upgrade copies missing defaults from there into ~/.config, and `omarchy-reinstall-configs` replays /etc/skel. The conclusion about existing Quattro installs is correct; only 'only through /etc/skel' is wrong.
flags.disposition: real error: 'ships only through /etc/skel'; fixed to list new accounts, reinstall-configs, v3 upgrade

flags.claim: Impact: The change mainly affects users who never install VS Code
flags.why: As worded, this claims an effect that does not exist. For users without VS Code the file does nothing: only the visual-studio-code-bin wrapper (and Arch's code-oss launcher) reads it. 'Mainly' is also a proportion I have no evidence for. My report said the file is harmless apart from finding 1 for accounts that never install VS Code.
flags.disposition: real error: 'mainly affects users who never install VS Code'; replaced with Opus wording

flags.claim: add a migration that sets `password-store` in an existing `~/.vscode/argv.json` when the key is absent, as open #8441 does for Cursor
flags.why: Part of the suggestion is missing. When Cursor is installed and argv.json is missing, #8441's migration also creates the file. A VS Code that was installed but never launched has no ~/.vscode/argv.json (VS Code creates the default file on first launch, without password-store), so a migration that only edits an existing file would skip it. My report had the same gap.
flags.disposition: real error: migration suggestion missed creating argv.json; fixed

flags.claim: VS Code reads `argv.json` only in the editor's main process (`configureCommandlineSwitchesSync` in `src/mainImpl.ts`), so the CLI subcommands never see it.
flags.why: Minor. The workbench also edits argv.json; for example, 'Use weaker encryption' writes password-store there through JSON editing. What the evidence supports: switches are applied in the main process at startup, cli.ts does not read argv.json, and the run shows `code tunnel status` works with the argv.json pin. This text is in my reproducer file, so a fix has to be made there and pasted again.
flags.disposition: real error in reproducer prose; fixed in reproducer file and draft

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The new `code-flags.conf` makes `code tunnel` and `code serve-web` fail, and Omarchy's VS Code installer already pins the same backend.

### `code tunnel` and `code serve-web` reject the appended flag

The AUR `/usr/bin/code` wrapper appends the file's flags after the user's arguments (`exec … "$@" $CODE_USER_FLAGS`). For `tunnel` and `serve-web`, VS Code forwards everything after the subcommand to its Rust CLI, which stops with `error: unexpected argument '--password-store' found`. **Impact:** `code tunnel …` and `code serve-web …` fail for every account seeded with the file, and the command still exits 0.

**Suggested change:** Drop `config/code-flags.conf` and keep the pin in `~/.vscode/argv.json`, which only the editor process reads.

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at de575fd)</summary>

## Reproducer: `config/code-flags.conf` breaks `code tunnel` and `code serve-web`

Tested at PR head `de575fd3af44002a438076945e4d035249eb9501` with the official VS Code 1.140.0 `.deb` (sha256 `e5ddfa52...0c3b`, the same file the AUR `visual-studio-code-bin` 1.140.0-1 PKGBUILD pins) and the AUR `/usr/bin/code` wrapper (`visual-studio-code-bin.sh`, unchanged since June 2026). The only change to the wrapper was pointing its `exec` at the extracted tree. It ran in an isolated sandbox with a throwaway `HOME`, no network and no display.

The AUR wrapper appends the lines of `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/code-flags.conf` after the user's arguments:

```bash
exec /usr/share/code/bin/code "$@" $CODE_USER_FLAGS
```

`code tunnel` / `code serve-web` forward every argument after the subcommand to the Rust `code-tunnel` binary. Its clap parser has no `--password-store` option.

### Steps (on a machine with `visual-studio-code-bin` installed)

```bash
empty=$(mktemp -d)
pr=$(mktemp -d)
printf '%s\n' '--password-store=gnome-libsecret' > "$pr/code-flags.conf"   # config/code-flags.conf from this PR

XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$empty" code tunnel status   # control: no flags file
XDG_CONFIG_HOME="$pr" code tunnel status      # with the PR's file
```

### Actual output

Control (`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` with no `code-flags.conf`):

```
stdout: {"tunnel":null,"service_installed":false}
exit status: 0
```

With the PR's `code-flags.conf`:

```
stderr:
error: unexpected argument '--password-store' found

Usage: code-tunnel tunnel status [OPTIONS]

For more information, try '--help'.
exit status: 0
```

The same file in `~/.config/code-flags.conf` (the path `/etc/skel` seeds) gives this for `code serve-web --without-connection-token --accept-server-license-terms --port 0`:

```
stderr:
error: unexpected argument '--password-store' found

Usage: code-tunnel serve-web --without-connection-token --accept-server-license-terms --port <PORT>

For more information, try '--help'.
exit status: 0
```

The wrapper still exits 0, so a script or unit that runs these commands does not see the failure.

This is the argument list the wrapper passes for `code tunnel status` with the PR's file. The `exec` target was replaced by an argv printer:

```
argv: [tunnel]
argv: [status]
argv: [--password-store=gnome-libsecret]
```

Comparison: a `~/.vscode/argv.json` containing `"password-store":"gnome-libsecret"` is what `omarchy-install-editor-vscode` already writes, and it has no `code-flags.conf`. With it, `code tunnel status` prints `{"tunnel":null,"service_installed":false}` and exits 0. VS Code applies `argv.json` switches only when the editor starts (`configureCommandlineSwitchesSync` in `src/mainImpl.ts`); the CLI subcommands never read it.
</details>

<details><summary>More findings</summary>

**The pin is already applied, and existing users do not get the file.**

`bin/omarchy-install-editor-vscode` already writes `"password-store":"gnome-libsecret"` to `~/.vscode/argv.json`, and that value overrides a command-line flag. The new file reaches only new accounts, `omarchy-reinstall-configs` and the one-time v3-to-Quattro upgrade. It does not reach existing Quattro installs where VS Code was added with pacman or yay. **Impact:** For VS Code installed through Omarchy the file adds nothing, and it misses the existing users it targets. It only helps new accounts that install VS Code with pacman or yay.

**Suggested change:** For VS Code installed outside the installer, add a migration that, when VS Code is installed, creates `~/.vscode/argv.json` with the pin or adds `password-store` when the key is absent, as open #8441 does for Cursor.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified:**
- The premise holds: Electron's sync OSCrypt selector maps Hyprland (`DESKTOP_ENVIRONMENT_OTHER`) to `basic_text` unless `--password-store=gnome-libsecret` is set (VS Code 1.139.1 and 1.140.0, Electron 43).
- Menu entries and the `vscode://` handler run through the wrapper, so the flag reaches the editor for ordinary launches.
- Arch's `code-oss` launcher also reads `code-flags.conf` but puts the flags before `"$@"`, so it is not affected by the tunnel failure.
- No conflict with the current `quattro` tip or with open #10346, #10018, #8441 or #10435.

**PR description:** The argv file VS Code reads is `~/.vscode/argv.json`, not `~/.config/Code/User/argv.json`.
</details>
